bug_semantics: AllowlistUnpickler (nltk/picklesec.py), the safer unpickler introduced for TransitionParser model loading and legacy Punkt pickle loading, restricts globals by WHOLE MODULE NAMESPACE: its `_module_allowed()` accepts any module equal to an allowed name or a submodule of one (`module == name or module.startswith(name + '.')`), and `find_class(module, name)` never inspects `name`. A pickle's REDUCE opcode can therefore reconstruct ANY callable reachable as an attribute of an allowed namespace: `_PUNKT_ALLOWED_MODULES = ('nltk.tokenize.punkt', 'nltk.tokenize')` exposes `nltk.tokenize.repp.ReppTokenizer._execute` (a static `subprocess.Popen` sink), and TransitionParser's `_MODEL_ALLOWED_MODULES = ('numpy', 'scipy', 'sklearn')` exposes `numpy.f2py.crackfortran.myeval` (an eval sink) — an attacker-supplied model/tokenizer artifact executes arbitrary commands during loading (CWE-502). Dotted-name chaining (pickle protocol >= 4) compounds the same defect: with `sklearn` allowed, `sklearn.os.system` resolves to os.system.
flaw_origin: Commit f26b3753038d937b68145daf15e9636f8451053c ("fix(security): prevent pickle RCE in TransitionParser model loading (CWE-502) (#3631)", 2026-07-01, author Litesh Ghute <61110758+LiteshGhute@users.noreply.github.com>, committer GitHub) wrote the entire vulnerable mechanism in one commit: the AllowlistUnpickler class in nltk/picklesec.py with the namespace-prefix `_module_allowed()` check and name-blind `find_class()`, PLUS both vulnerable wirings — `_PUNKT_ALLOWED_MODULES = ('nltk.tokenize.punkt', 'nltk.tokenize')` in punkt.py and `allowed_modules=_MODEL_ALLOWED_MODULES` in transitionparser.py. Its docstring promises os.system 'can never be reconstructed' while the prefix allow structurally permits in-namespace gadgets. Prior state used unrestricted pickle loading (warn-and-execute); the named sink — the allowlisted loader that trusts whole namespaces — is born here.
